observations.text: SP maintained a visual check of the surrounding space at the level expected for this training unit, with the IP directing when and where to look before each maneuver and in the airport traffic pattern. Nearby moving A/C were acquired only after they were pointed out from the rear cockpit, and R/T reports were heard but were not correlated with the traffic picture without assistance. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent allocation of attention between A/C control and the outside scan is expected to develop in the following sorties.

SP checked the surrounding space and cleared the area before each maneuver after verbal prompts from the IP, with no part of the visual check having to be directed or executed from the rear cockpit. Traffic reported on the R/T was correlated with the outside picture with delay, and the required clearing turn was initiated late but by SP alone. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP checked the surrounding space continuously through the working phase of the sortie and detected the nearby moving A/C in the overhead pattern without prompting. The scan lapsed briefly during the entry to one maneuver, and SP recognized the omission and flew the clearing turn before rolling in, in a timely manner and without IP's intervention. Appropriate separation from the reported traffic and appropriate VFR distance from clouds were maintained throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP allocated attention correctly between A/C control and the outside scan, checking the surrounding space uninterruptedly and particularly in the airport traffic pattern. Nearby moving A/C were detected in good time, appropriate separation was maintained and the R/T was monitored continuously, so that the traffic picture was built without IP's intervention. Appropriate VFR distance from clouds was maintained at every point of the profile. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained an uninterrupted check of the surrounding space while keeping the A/C under control at all times, with the scan reorganized ahead of each maneuver entry and each pattern entry. Two A/C were acquired visually before their position reports were made on the R/T, appropriate separation was established early and no avoidance maneuver was required at any point. Monitoring of the R/T was used to anticipate the traffic sequence rather than to react to it, and appropriate VFR distance from clouds was maintained with margin. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a scan pattern held inside the cockpit for long intervals, could not maintain the required check of the surrounding space without assistance and did not clear the area before entering the maneuvers. The result was that the IP had to direct the visual check and call the nearby moving A/C in the airport traffic pattern. Further work on the division of attention between A/C control and the outside scan is required.

SP, due to attention captured by a single cockpit indication while the outside scan went unmonitored, did not check the surrounding space during the working phase and did not correlate the R/T reports with the traffic picture. The result was that the IP had to direct the lookout and execute the avoidance turn when separation from the reported A/C reduced. Recovery of the scan followed the IP's direction and was not initiated by SP.

SP performed the clearing at the level expected for this training unit, checking the surrounding space and flying the clearing turns after verbal prompts from the IP. Nearby moving A/C were detected and appropriate separation was restored with delay, although no part of the check had to be executed by the IP. Marginal performance for the Training Section - timely detection of traffic without prompting is expected to improve in the following sorties.

SP checked the surrounding space through the sortie and detected the nearby moving A/C on the downwind without prompting from the rear cockpit. The scan was interrupted once while a cockpit switch was being reset, and SP recognized the interruption and re-established the outside check before the next maneuver, without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP allocated attention correctly, keeping the check of the surrounding space uninterrupted while the A/C was maintained under control, and cleared the area accurately before every maneuver. Traffic reported on the R/T was identified visually in good time and appropriate separation was maintained without any avoidance maneuver becoming necessary. Appropriate VFR distance from clouds was maintained throughout the working phase. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained an uninterrupted visual check of the surrounding space, with the scan deliberately widened before each maneuver entry and on every leg of the airport traffic pattern. All reported traffic was acquired visually before it became a factor, appropriate separation was established early and the A/C was kept under control at every point of the profile. Continuous monitoring of the R/T was used to build the traffic picture ahead of the sequence, and appropriate VFR distance from clouds was maintained with margin. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a lookout confined to the sector ahead of the nose, could not maintain the required check of the surrounding space without assistance and did not clear the sectors behind and above before the maneuvers. The result was that the IP had to direct the scan and initiate the separation turn from the traffic joining the pattern. Systematic coverage of the whole surrounding space, and not only of the sector in front, is required.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while positioning for the next maneuver, did not check the surrounding space and did not detect the A/C converging from the left. The result was that the IP had to call the traffic and execute the avoidance maneuver to restore appropriate separation. The R/T was heard but was not used to build the traffic picture, and the scan was resumed only after the IP's direction.

SP, due to a clearing turn flown too shallow to expose the area behind the A/C, did not check the whole surrounding space before the maneuver entry and did not detect the traffic operating in the working area. The nearby A/C was acquired only after the IP's verbal prompt, and appropriate separation was restored by SP with delay but without intervention on the controls. Coverage of the blind sectors during the clearing turn is to be reworked.

SP, due to workload distribution that left navigation, the R/T call and A/C control attempted at the same time, did not maintain the uninterrupted check of the surrounding space on entry to the airport traffic pattern. Traffic already reported on the R/T was recognized only after the IP's verbal prompt, and the correction required to re-establish appropriate separation was applied with delay. No intervention on the controls was needed, but the traffic picture was rebuilt after prompting rather than by SP alone.

SP performed the clearing within the desired standards, checking the surrounding space during flight and detecting the nearby moving A/C in time to maintain appropriate separation. The scan was interrupted twice while the A/C was being repositioned between maneuvers, and on both occasions SP recognized the interruption and re-established the outside check without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - continuity of the visual check while handling the A/C between maneuvers is expected to improve.

SP allocated attention accurately between A/C control and the outside scan, checking the surrounding space uninterruptedly and particularly on every leg of the airport traffic pattern. Nearby moving A/C were detected quickly, appropriate separation was maintained and continuous monitoring of the R/T supported a complete traffic picture without IP's intervention. Appropriate VFR distance from clouds was maintained at every point of the working phase. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP kept the check of the surrounding space uninterrupted through the whole sortie, including the transitions between maneuvers where the scan is most often lost, and the A/C remained under control at all times. Three A/C operating in the adjacent area were identified from their R/T reports and tracked visually, so that appropriate separation was planned in advance and no avoidance maneuver was required. The clearing turns were flown to expose the sectors behind and above the A/C, and appropriate VFR distance from clouds was maintained with margin. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a visual check limited to short glances that did not cover the sectors above and behind, could not clear the surrounding space without assistance during the working phase of the sortie. The result was that the IP had to direct the lookout before each maneuver and execute the separation turn from the A/C entering the area. A systematic scan sequence covering the whole surrounding space is to be built before the next sortie.

SP, due to lack of any agreed division of lookout responsibility between the two cockpits, did not check the sectors that had not been covered from the rear seat and did not report the traffic that had already been called on the R/T. The result was that the IP had to direct the visual check and take the A/C to restore appropriate separation from the converging traffic in the pattern. The division of lookout responsibility is to be stated explicitly before the working phase.

SP, due to a scan rhythm that stopped whenever the A/C was being trimmed and repositioned, did not check the surrounding space uninterruptedly between the maneuvers of the working phase. Nearby moving A/C were detected only after the IP's verbal prompts, and appropriate separation was restored with delay, without intervention on the controls. Continuity of the outside check while handling the A/C is to be reworked.

SP, due to complacency in a familiar pattern that replaced an active scan, did not check the surrounding space uninterruptedly in the airport traffic pattern and did not correlate the position reports on the R/T with the A/C in sight. The traffic on the opposite downwind was recognized only after the IP's verbal prompt, and the extension of the downwind that restored appropriate separation was applied with delay. No intervention on the controls was required, but the traffic picture was completed after prompting rather than by SP alone.

SP, due to a clearing turn started before the outside references had been reacquired after the previous maneuver, left one sector of the surrounding space unchecked at the entry to the aerobatic block. SP recognized the gap, repeated the clearing turn and confirmed the area clear before rolling in, in a timely manner and without IP's intervention. Appropriate separation and appropriate VFR distance from clouds were maintained throughout the remainder of the sortie.

SP, due to sun glare in the sector into which the A/C was turning, did not detect the reported traffic on the first sweep of the surrounding space during the recovery to the field. SP recognized the omission, offset the heading to move the search sector out of the sun and acquired the A/C in time to maintain appropriate separation, without IP's intervention. The error was minor and monitoring of the R/T remained continuous through the recovery.

SP performed the clearing within the desired standards, checking the surrounding space during flight and in the airport traffic pattern and maintaining appropriate separation from all reported traffic without IP's intervention. The visual check before two maneuver entries was completed slowly, so that the roll-in followed the clearing turn later than the profile requires, and at those points the R/T picture was rebuilt rather than kept current. Marginal performance for the Training Section - speed of the visual check is expected to improve while the present accuracy of the scan is maintained.

SP checked the surrounding space uninterruptedly and kept the A/C under control at every point of the profile, with the clearing turns flown to expose the sectors behind and above before each maneuver entry. All traffic operating in the area was acquired visually and correlated with the R/T reports as they were made, so that appropriate separation was planned in advance and no avoidance maneuver became necessary. Appropriate VFR distance from clouds was maintained with margin, and the outside picture was passed to the rear cockpit at every change of the traffic situation. Above end of block MIF achieved.
